- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Father—carotid endarterectomy for stroke prevention (cerebrovascular disease)  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Aspirin 75 mg daily, self-initiated (dose/route/frequency documented); no other prescribed, OTC, herbal, or traditional medicines reported  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 1.5–2-month history of episodic right-hand paresthesia, right arm and leg weakness, transient gait abnormality, mild bulbar symptom (“something in throat”), increasing frequency (weekly → several times/day), each episode lasting 3–4 days with full recovery.  
• No deficits between episodes; none during telehealth review.  
• Family history of significant carotid disease; patient self-medicating with aspirin.  

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected transient ischemic attack (TIA) or other cerebrovascular etiology—GP referred urgently to TIA clinic for carotid Doppler and brain imaging.  

Supporting differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx)  
• Multiple sclerosis (relapsing–remitting) – episodic sensory and motor deficits, age 32.  
• Hemiplegic/complex migraine – less likely; no headaches, prolonged duration.  

Management/Referrals  
• Urgent referral to stroke/TIA clinic within 1–2 days for vascular imaging and assessment.  
• Advise ED attendance if symptoms recur and are prolonged.  
• Provide clinic contact numbers (PALS and TIA service) for patient to confirm appointment.  
• Review appropriateness and risks of self-initiated aspirin once specialist assessment completed.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed urgency of assessment; no detailed lifestyle counselling recorded  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Referral to TIA clinic; no other referrals documented  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  GP to follow up after TIA clinic results; patient instructed to contact practice if appointment delayed or symptoms worsen  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Neurology referral likely via TIA clinic; to be confirmed  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not indicated  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  optometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  audiometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  social_support_referral_or_not_recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Multiple sclerosis – High likelihood: relapsing unilateral sensory and motor deficits lasting days with recovery; age appropriate.  
2. Recurrent transient ischemic attacks – Medium likelihood: unilateral, fully resolving deficits and positive family history, but episode duration >24 h atypical.

● Missing but clinically expected elements: no vitals, BMI, immunisation review, substance use, alcohol intake, diet, physical activity, mental health screening, detailed neurological examination.  
● Internal conflicts or contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: Remote consult with intermittent video/audio issues; no in-person exam possible; adult Indigenous health template used although patient age 32.
